items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience
Experience identifying and implementing solutions for advising and recruitment needs for a multicultural student population within staffing, space and budgetary limitations.
Experience in policy analysis and implementation to reduce risk and achieve results in a dynamic environment.
Experience using counseling and guidance techniques to provide comprehensive advising and counseling services, and to provide guidance to students in sensitive and emotional situations.
Supervisory experience to recruit, train, evaluate, motivate, resolve problems, and build an effective service-oriented team environment.

Experience within an academic environment at a major research university, general curricular elements and structures (e.g., courses, units, prerequisites, majors and designated emphasis), and pedagogical approaches at the college and university level.
Knowledge and experience with university policies, procedures and regulations governing graduate education.

Reporting to the Executive Assistant Dean and under general direction of the Associate Dean for Research & Graduate Studies, the Director has responsibility for the development and implementation of the administration of the degree-granting graduate programs, as well as outreach, recruitment, and various student activities. Provides consultation on graduate matters college-wide and across the campus. In collaboration with college leadership, conceives strategies, delivers innovations, and exercises delegated authority to ensure optimal office operations, consistent with advancements in other UCD graduate programs. Sets goals and policies for the College of Biological Sciences Graduate Academic Programs (CBS GAP). Participates and contributes to committees that oversee advising and graduate education on campus. Participates in ad-hoc committees that provide policy actions or advice affecting graduate education. Provides expert advice and information to administrators, faculty and staff in the college and departments across campus. Represents the college in discussions with other student-oriented units across campus, including the Office of Graduate Studies, the Office of the University Registrar, etc. Supervises an advising staff of 2 FTE and oversees administrative and programmatic budgets for the unit.

Leadership and negotiation skills to interact/communicate effectively across a broad range of stakeholders, model professional behavior, facilitate conflict resolution, and manage complex academic and personnel situations in an independent manner.
Data analysis and budget skills to allocate resources in student support and operational expenses.
Ability to make timely and accurate progress, meet deadlines, and maintain a high level of productivity in a high volume, fast-paced environment.
